#### 1. X-linked spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.762)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3560783, Reactome:R-HSA-2022870, Reactome:R-HSA-2022923, Reactome:R-HSA-3560801, Reactome:R-HSA-3595177)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic BGN variant (MONDO:0010515) —DISRUPTS→ BIGLYCAN (HGNC:1044); Pathogenic BGN variant (MONDO:0010248) —DISRUPTS→ BIGLYCAN (HGNC:1044); BIGLYCAN (HGNC:1044) —DECREASES→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0004325); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Joint hypermobility (HP:0001382). Loss-of-function mutations in the BIGLYCAN (BGN) gene disrupt extracellular matrix organization, leading to skeletal dysplasia and joint hypermobility, which are characteristic phenotypes of both Meester-Loeys syndrome and X-linked spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in BGN that are consistently loss-of-function in one disease but gain-of-function or dominant-negative in the other, or the absence of any shared phenotypic features between patients with documented BGN mutations. _(variant: Any common (AF > 0.01) loss-of-function variants in BGN observed in gnomAD that do not segregate with either Meester-Loeys syndrome or X-linked spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of BGN in these distinct yet overlapping syndromes could facilitate the development of targeted therapies for matrix-related skeletal disorders, potentially by modulating extracellular matrix composition or turnover.
